venue.name: Itabashi City Cultural Hall — Small Hall

events.category: Living jazz master / tenor saxophone and flute trio / Japan tour
events.factual_description: The Itabashi Culture and International Exchange Foundation presents Lew Tabackin Trio Japan Tour 2026 in ITABASHI on Monday, September 21, 2026 at Itabashi City Cultural Hall's Small Hall, with doors at 13:00 and the performance at 14:00. The announced trio is Lew Tabackin on tenor saxophone and flute, Motoi Kanamori on bass, and Shinnosuke Takahashi on drums. The published program includes John Lewis's “Afternoon in Paris,” Tabackin originals “Garden at Lifetime,” “BFlat,” and “Sakura Princess,” Michael Moore's “The Lilter,” Don Byas's “Gloria,” and John Coltrane's “Wise One,” with the program subject to change. All seating is reserved at a listed general price of ¥4,000. The organizer's official page lists ticket sales through the cultural hall, its web system, Ticket Pia and district ticket outlets.

en.why_it_matters: The point is the exposed two-instrument voice, not the legend label. Tabackin can move between tenor and flute over a bass-and-drums trio with nowhere for the articulation to hide, and the published program links John Lewis, Don Byas and Coltrane to his own writing. His long musical history with Japan gives the local rhythm section and the Itabashi setting real continuity rather than the feel of a generic overseas stop.
en.trip_verdict: If Tokyo is already in play on September 21, actively make room for the Itabashi matinee and build the afternoon around the Small Hall. I would not make it a special-trip anchor by itself because the same trio is touring Japan on multiple dates.

es.why_it_matters: La razón está en esa voz instrumental expuesta, no en la etiqueta de leyenda. Tabackin puede pasar del tenor a la flauta sobre un trío de bajo y batería sin que la articulación tenga dónde esconderse, y el programa publicado conecta a John Lewis, Don Byas y Coltrane con composiciones propias. Su larga historia musical con Japón le da continuidad real a la sección rítmica local y al contexto de Itabashi, en vez de sentirse como una parada genérica de gira.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio ya está en juego el 21 de septiembre, sí le haría espacio al matiné de Itabashi y armaría la tarde alrededor de la sala pequeña. No lo convertiría por sí solo en ancla de un viaje especial porque el mismo trío recorre varias ciudades de Japón.

events.factual_description: JZ Brat Sound of Tokyo presents Yuka Sasaki Quartet with David Matthews and special guest Lew Tabackin on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, with doors at 18:00 and the performance at 19:00; the venue schedules an intermission and a 21:30 finish with no audience turnover. The announced lineup is Yuka Sasaki on flute, Satoshi Inoue on guitar, Iwao Masuhara on bass, Kazuaki Yokoyama on percussion, David Matthews on piano, and Lew Tabackin on tenor saxophone and flute. JZ Brat notes that Sasaki studied in New York with Tabackin and explicitly foregrounds their flute exchanges. Front-row S seating is listed at ¥8,000 and is sold out; general reservation is ¥7,000 and the door charge is ¥7,500, before the venue's service charge.

en.why_it_matters: The reason to include this one is the mentor-student instrument conversation. Sasaki puts her flute directly beside the teacher she sought out in New York; Tabackin can answer on flute or pivot to tenor, while David Matthews and the guitar/bass/percussion quartet widen the harmonic and rhythmic palette without turning the appearance into a generic guest spot.
en.trip_verdict: If Shibuya is already part of the Wednesday plan and the evening is open, this is worth choosing. The same Sasaki/Matthews/Tabackin project is touring elsewhere, so I would fit it around stronger one-off Tokyo anchors rather than reorganize the trip around it.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para meter esta fecha es la conversación instrumental entre maestra y discípula. Sasaki pone su flauta directamente junto al maestro que buscó en Nueva York; Tabackin puede responder con flauta o cambiar al tenor, mientras David Matthews y el cuarteto de guitarra, bajo y percusión amplían el color armónico y rítmico sin convertir la aparición en un simple guest spot.
es.trip_verdict: Si Shibuya ya forma parte del plan del miércoles y la noche está libre, vale escoger esta fecha. El mismo proyecto Sasaki/Matthews/Tabackin está de gira por otras ciudades, así que lo acomodaría alrededor de anclas más irrepetibles de Tokio en vez de reorganizar el viaje por él.
